reason: COVID-19 and digitalization did change how people live and how sport is performed and consumed, so sport did not escape societal shock. But French and other participation series also show continuity and later recovery or even a slight rise in regular sport after 2018, so lifestyles and sport were not generally “deeply transformed” as a lasting, across-the-board result by 2026-11-15.
quote: our lifestyles are likely to be deeply transformed. Sport will not escape such challenges
claim: Whatever strategy societies adopt, lifestyles are likely to be deeply transformed, and sport will not escape those challenges.

reason: UNESCO and some governments continued to expand futures-literacy and foresight work after 2018, including World Futures Day 2025 and a Global Anticipatory Policy coalition, which supports a direction of greater currency. Independent public-management research in 2026 still finds strategic foresight largely marginal, so the stated endpoint of far greater currency and impact has not been reached.
quote: we are beginning to make out a not too distant future in which futures thinking enjoys far greater currency and impact, by becoming not only more accessible – but also more fun.
claim: A not-too-distant future is coming in which futures thinking enjoys far greater currency and impact, becoming more accessible and more fun.

reason: A 2025 systematic review and other studies still disagree on whether filter bubbles and echo chambers exist, intensified, or usefully describe most users’ media diets. Because the claimed strengthening of both global communication and Filter Bubble limits is empirically contested, the claim cannot be scored on the archived record.
quote: two contradictory occurrences are expected to continue and become even stronger in the future.
claim: The two contradictory occurrences (expanded global communication and the Filter Bubble limiting awareness) are expected to continue and become even stronger in the future.

reason: Search and generative-AI tools after 2018 made desired information quicker to reach, and work on the “narrow search effect” supports comfort- or confirmation-bounded knowing. But reviews also show information overload and weaker science learning on social media, so it is not established that people “know more overall.”
quote: We will most likely know more overall in the future and will be able to find desired information very quickly, but the knowing will be bounded by the doing of what feels emotionally comfortable and safe.
claim: People will most likely know more overall in the future and find desired information very quickly, but that knowing will be bounded by doing what feels emotionally comfortable and safe.

reason: The condition only partly holds. ILGA and other records show expanded legal gender recognition in some jurisdictions, while CIVICUS, ILGA-Europe and reporting on the United States document a sharp 2020s rollback and repression of gender-fluid and trans rights in others. Where the condition holds, civic space is more constrained; it is not a uniform global “stifled present.”
quote: as long as gendered fluidity is repressed and penalised, and as long as our future imaginings are based on one-dimensional gender identities where ‘men are men’ and ‘women are women’, our future presents will remain stifled and limiting.
claim: If gendered fluidity remains repressed and penalised and future imaginings stay based on one-dimensional ‘men are men’ / ‘women are women’ identities, future presents will remain stifled and limiting.

reason: Feminist and LGBTQ-inclusive policy work continued in some international and national settings after 2018, so a push toward more inclusive futures is visible. The same window also shows a documented global backlash and rollback of gender justice, so that push does not unambiguously continue as the dominant direction.
quote: the influence of postmodern as well as feminist theories will continue to push towards such futures.
claim: The influence of postmodern and feminist theories, together with related social-rights and communication trends, will continue to push towards more inclusive and equitable futures.

reason: Democratic backsliding, conservative and ‘green’ backlash, and climate-policy strain after 2018 are well documented and pull toward less equitable climate and civic outcomes. International IDEA and other sources do not show a general economic or ecological collapse, so that half of the claim is not borne out.
quote: economic and ecological collapse, increases in social conservatism and fundamentalism, various forms of backlash against socially progressive movements and ideas will continue to act as both our ‘weight of history’ and a detrimental pull towards inequitable futures.
claim: Economic and ecological collapse, rising social conservatism and fundamentalism, and backlash against socially progressive movements will continue to act as a weight of history and a pull towards inequitable futures.
